expl.summary: This formula is built without any jet-mass observable: the if-statements use only shape, energy-correlation, subjet and particle-pT quantities, so mass information enters only through ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² (Σ zᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ², which approximates (m/pT)² at small angles), e₂, ΣzΔR, ΣzΔR² and λ₁+λ₂. Each of the 16 neurons is a clipped sum of if-statements on these quantities, and each class score adds some neurons and subtracts others; the formula reaches a validation accuracy of 65.45%. The t score is dominated by jet size: it subtracts neuron 13 (ΣzΔR < 0.148, -48%), on which t jets average 0.985 against 3.6-4.4 for all other classes, and adds neuron 10 (linear in λ₁, +26%), so it follows ΣzΔR and λ₁+λ₂ with rank correlations of 0.926 and 0.923. The q score takes 55% of its input from neuron 9 (narrow jets at lower total pT) and subtracts neuron 10 (-18%); the g score takes 38% from neuron 2, which rises with the pT of the 8th-hardest particle and falls with jet mass (rank correlation -0.73), plus neuron 9 (+22%), and subtracts neuron 5 (small angularity, pT in the few hardest particles, -14%). Both two-prong scores add neuron 7 (elongated jets with moderate ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ²; +35% for Z, +13% for W) and subtract neurons 3 and 6 (pT at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4, broad off-centre spread). W and Z are separated without a mass variable by narrow windows in ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² and ΣzΔR²: neuron 11 (λ₁+λ₂ < 0.0132 but not the narrowest jets) enters only the W score (+24%), neuron 14 (ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² between about 0.00718 and 0.0117) adds to the Z score (+6%) and subtracts from the W score (-10%), and neuron 15 (ΣzΔR² between 0.00752 and 0.0132) takes more out of the W score (-8%) than out of the Z score (-2%).
